caveats:
This product contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2025), processed by ESA and analyzed by the Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS).

These are preliminary maps derived from satellite radar and should be used as guidance only. Coloured pixels may include false positives, and their absence does not mean an absence of damage or flooding.
methodology_other: Change detection on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images acquired before and after the event. Damage Proxy Maps show significant changes in radar coherence and amplitude; Flood Proxy Maps show areas that changed to standing water. Maps are preliminary and checked against news reports and ground-level imagery where available.

# Philippines Typhoon Fung-Wong: Damage and Flood Proxy Maps, Nov 2025

The **Earth Observatory of Singapore – Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS)** produced these damage and flood proxy maps for Philippines Typhoon Fung-Wong (Nov 2025) from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images. Each map is a separate ZIP below with its GeoTIFF, a KMZ for Google Earth, the PNG figures and a text file describing how it was made and how to read it.

## Maps in this dataset

- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Eastern Luzon, Philippines, Typhoon Fung-Wong, 11 Nov 2025, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Flood Proxy Map: Eastern Luzon, Philippines, Typhoon Fung-Wong, 11 Nov 2025, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Bicol and Eastern Visayas, Philippines, Typhoon Fung-Wong, 10 Nov 2025, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Bicol Region, Philippines, Typhoon Fung-Wong, 09 Nov 2025, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Flood Proxy Map: Bicol Region, Philippines, Typhoon Fung-Wong, 09 Nov 2025, v0.9**

**More map details and files:** <https://sf.earthobservatory.sg/event/EOS-RS_202511_Philippines_Typhoon_Fung-Wong>

**Legal Disclaimer:** <https://sf.earthobservatory.sg/faq/>

**Credits:** Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS), Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2025)

organization.title: Earth Observatory of Singapore
organization.description: The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) is a research lab at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. It uses satellite remote sensing, mainly synthetic aperture radar (SAR), to map natural hazards and disasters. The lab produces Damage Proxy Maps (DPMs) and Flood Proxy Maps (FPMs) showing where damage or flooding has likely occurred. Its work focuses on Southeast Asia and the wider Asia-Pacific, and it also responds to major disasters worldwide.

resources.description:
EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Eastern Luzon, Philippines, Typhoon Fung-Wong, 11 Nov 2025, v0.9

ZIP containing: GeoTIFF, KMZ, PNG, TXT.

The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) created this preliminary Damage Proxy Map (DPM) depicting areas that are likely damaged in in Eastern Luzon, Philippines, due to Typhoon Fung-Wong. Typhoon Fung-Wong made landfall in Dinalungan, Aurora at 13:10 UTC on 09 November 2025 as a super typhoon. This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellite operated by the European Space Agency (ESA) before (03 May 2025 to 30 Oct 2025) and after (11 Nov 2025) the event.
